what: The Races — the register Parallelogram tracks. A race is a seat with two conditional Readings (data/readings/races/), each authored z-first by the twelve stations and paid on election day: one collapses into the live Reading, the other is retired as the record of the miss. Polling enters as outcome weight only, never as z. The record is the candidates' actual legislative objects; the trail is what they said, paid after. Each candidate also carries a second needle, gap{talk, done, line}: what they say scored the same way as the needle, against what their record has done — Claude drafts, 2026-10-12.

races.object: The seat. A six-year instrument held since 1997 by the only Republican senator in a state that has voted against Trump three times.
races.question: Does Maine's seat deliver the thing Maine asked for — rent, insulin, the shipyard — or does it deliver a vote to a caucus?
races.rating: Tossup (Cook, Sabato) · Lean D (Economist, Silver Bulletin, Split Ticket) — as of late September

gap.line: She says Maine first and independent of the party. Her record: she did cross her party on the big spending bill, the rescissions and the health-insurance rule — but she voted for the Iran sanctions bill and every funding bill with everyone else. The independence is real on money; it stops at war.

candidates.name: Troy Jackson
candidates.role: Logger from Allagash · Maine Senate President 2018–2024 · nominated at convention 2026-07-25 after Graham Platner withdrew

gap.line: He says lower costs, no more war money, stand with workers. His record is twenty years in Augusta with real bills passed — school meals, drug prices — and no vote yet on a war or a tariff, because he has never had one. The gap is untested, not broken.

jackson.title: Twenty years in the Maine Legislature; Senate President 2018–2024 (six years)
jackson.read: The record is a state record: universal school meals, prescription-drug pricing, reproductive-health protections, property-tax relief — as his campaign states them. Bill numbers owed from LegiScan.

jackson.title: The loggers' blockade against wage-cutting landowners (late 1990s)
jackson.read: His founding story, and it names her: a first-term Senator Collins promised to listen and didn't. The race, told by him, is that blockade thirty years on.

trail.note: Said on the trail — positions as hypotheses, paid after the vote. verbatim:false means the position is sourced but not quoted.

rows.said: Collins has been in Washington thirty years and sides with Trump when it counts.
rows.pays: If Jackson wins and votes with his own caucus on the first CR with war money, the line pays against him.

rows.said: Maine first: the seat on Appropriations is the seat that brings the money home.
rows.pays: Measurable on the FY27 appropriations if she holds; a +24 issue lead is the base's expectation, not a z.

rows.said: Voted alone to disapprove the ACA payment rule — the only Republican.
rows.pays: A roll call, already paid: 48–51. The question the paper asks is whether a lone vote is a delivery or a signal.

races.object: The seat John Cornyn held since 2002 and lost in a runoff. No Democrat has won it, or any Texas Senate seat, since 1988.
races.question: Does Texas's seat deliver — vouchers, insulin, the Valley, the lawsuits — or is it a thirty-eight-year habit on the ballot?
races.rating: Tilt R (Inside Elections) · RCP average Talarico +2.8 (9/18–10/8)

candidates.name: Ken Paxton
candidates.role: Texas Attorney General since 2015 · beat Cornyn in the 2026-05-26 runoff, 64–36 · Trump endorsed 05-19

gap.line: He says he fights for Texans against Washington. His record as Attorney General is lawsuits — including one to throw his own opponent out of the Legislature, which the state Supreme Court threw out instead. Nothing on his record lowers a cost or ends a war.

candidates.name: James Talarico
candidates.role: Texas State Representative, HD-50, since 2019 · seminarian · won the 03-03 primary outright, 52%, over Rep. Jasmine Crockett

gap.line: He says insulin, schools, no vouchers. His record: one law with his name on it (the $25 insulin cap) and three fights lost on the floor — vouchers, the Ten Commandments bill, the THC ban. The talk and the record point the same way; most of the record is losses.
